html:
The Lapita culture arose in the Bismarck Archipelago of New Guinea about 3,300 years ago; Watom island, off New Britain, is one of its early sites. Its people made pottery stamped with fine toothed patterns and sailed east into islands no one had reached before.

Within a few centuries they reached Vanuatu, New Caledonia, Fiji, Tonga and Samoa, bringing pigs, dogs, chickens and crops. The culture is named after a site in New Caledonia dug in 1952.

They came from Austronesian seafarers out of Island Southeast Asia, who mixed with Papuan peoples of the Bismarcks. Their descendants became the Polynesians who later settled the rest of the Pacific. See the Lapita voyagers.
